economy.summary: In her April 2026 candidacy announcement, listed addressing the rising cost of living and supporting agriculture among her campaign priorities, saying her campaign is about meeting people where they are and working together to solve problems.
economy.short: Lists addressing rising cost of living, supporting agriculture as priorities.

education.summary: In her candidacy announcement, listed investing in education and trade programs among her campaign priorities; her campaign site cites school funding shortfalls as a challenge facing the district.
education.short: Proposes investing in education and trade programs.

healthcare.summary: In a campaign-site article on the closure of Tyler Memorial Hospital, opposes the Medicaid reductions in the 2025 federal reconciliation law, saying they will affect more than 300,000 Pennsylvanians in rural communities, and calls for leaders who stand up for rural health.
healthcare.short: Opposes federal Medicaid cuts; calls for protecting rural healthcare.

economy.summary: In a joint statement with Rep. Owlett on the 2025-26 state budget, said it will unleash opportunities for new construction, manufacturing, data centers and family-sustaining jobs across the Northern Tier and the state.
economy.short: Says budget supports construction, manufacturing, data centers, family-sustaining jobs.

taxes.summary: Supported House passage of the 2026-27 state budget, saying it brought spending down to $50.8 billion while avoiding new taxes and leaving the state's Rainy Day Fund intact, while noting it was not a budget she would have written herself.
taxes.short: Backed budget avoiding new taxes, preserving Rainy Day Fund.

abortion.summary: Voted in July 2022 for Senate Bill 106, a package of proposed constitutional amendments that included a provision stating the Pennsylvania Constitution does not grant any right relating to abortion or to public funding of abortion.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment stating constitution grants no abortion right.

education.summary: In a joint statement with Rep. Owlett on the 2025-26 state budget, supported doubling scholarship funding for students who attend economically disadvantaged schools, saying kids only get one chance at a good education.
education.short: Supports doubling scholarships for students in disadvantaged schools.

healthcare.summary: Sponsored House Bill 2419, signed into law as Act 76 of 2022, which expands telehealth options for mental health treatment by removing the requirement that half of psychiatric care occur on-site, saying telemedicine makes mental health treatment more available to clinics and doctors.
healthcare.short: Sponsored law expanding telehealth for mental health treatment.

energy.summary: In a joint statement with Rep. Owlett on the 2025-26 state budget, highlighted removing Pennsylvania from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative and streamlining permit approvals as crucial for meeting regional energy needs and creating jobs.
energy.short: Supports leaving RGGI and streamlining energy permit approvals.

guns.summary: Voted in November 2021 for Senate Bill 565, which would have removed the license requirement for carrying a concealed firearm in Pennsylvania; the bill passed the House 107-92 and was later vetoed by the governor.
guns.short: Voted to remove concealed carry license requirement.
